sections.h2: Choices for selling a Stockbridge house
sections.html:
A Stockbridge owner heading for the exit can use an agent, go it alone, or field a straight offer from a buyer with cash in hand. The open market puts the house in front of the most bidders. A direct deal gives up some of that competition and gets speed and fewer strings in return.

  • An agent's listing suits a sound house whose owner can wait out the bank's review of the buyer.
  • Going without an agent works for owners who can price a house, screen callers and run a contract.
  • Cash buyers fit homes with deferred repairs, delinquent taxes, a renter or an unsettled estate.

Whichever you choose, Henry County property tax and a state transfer tax come into play, and the sections below name the offices that handle each.

More than half of Stockbridge households own. The 2020 to 2024 tables show a 56.0 percent ownership rate across 14,320 households, and the July 2025 estimate of 36,331 residents follows counts of 28,973 in 2020 and 25,636 in 2010. Stockbridge lies near I-75, I-675 and Hartsfield-Jackson Atlanta International Airport, so say in your description how many minutes your house is from those roads.

sections.h2: Roads and services buyers ask about
sections.html:
Commuters check the route to I-75 first. State transportation authority park and ride lots sit just north of I-75 at State Route 138 and off Mount Zion Parkway, and Xpress bus routes leave from Stockbridge.

  • Rock Quarry Road is getting four lanes in place of two along a 2.6 mile stretch from Eagles Landing Parkway to SR 138, also called US 23 and North Henry Boulevard, to relieve traffic near Piedmont Henry Hospital.
  • Fire and medical calls go to Henry County Fire Station 9 on Rock Quarry Road, and the city has its own police department.
  • Henry County Schools operate the public schools, and the Cochran Public Library stands on Burke Street.

sections.h2: How does Henry County property tax work for a Stockbridge seller?
sections.html:
The Henry County tax commissioner sends each bill to the January 1 owner, with payment due by November 16. Late balances accrue interest and penalties under a schedule printed in the county's FAQ, and a mailed payment needs a USPS postmark.

A sale that closes mid-year needs one extra step. Under Georgia Code 48-3-3, a lien lands on the January 1 owner unless the county receives a settlement statement showing where the taxes were paid within 90 days after the due date. Henry County wants page one of that statement and the property address, sent to its property tax email.

Fees can surprise a seller. Streetlight, stormwater and sanitation charges ride on the same bill, and a county water charge pays for pipes and storage even if a house has a well. The departments named on the bill answer questions about each fee.

Homestead applications in Henry County are due April 1 and can be made online or at either tax office, one on Burke Street in Stockbridge and the main office on Henry Parkway in McDonough. Bring a license showing the home address, vehicle registrations at that address, the warranty deed, and a divorce decree where one applies.

  • A married couple gets homestead on one residence only.
  • Henry County offers a homestead valuation freeze.
  • An appeal of the assessment must carry a postmark within 45 days of the notice.

Owners who have fallen behind face tax sales that the county runs on the first Tuesday of each month, starting at 10:00 AM at the McDonough office on Henry Parkway.

A Stockbridge seller who is behind on taxes still has options. Because the bill follows the January 1 owner, an unpaid balance can lead to a lien and, in time, to one of the monthly tax sales. Paying the balance out of sale proceeds at closing is the usual fix, and a closing attorney can arrange it when the payoff is listed on the settlement statement.

A cash buyer often fits here, since the sale does not wait on a lender's review of the property. Ask each buyer how the tax payoff will be handled, who pays any penalty and interest, and whether the closing date leaves enough room to deliver the settlement statement to the county in time. Call the tax commissioner for the exact figure first, so an offer is judged against the real balance and not a guess.

sections.h2: Transfer steps at a Stockbridge closing
sections.html:
Before a Stockbridge deed is recorded, the state's transfer tax has to be paid. The seller bears it unless the contract names the buyer, and the Department of Revenue lists the current rate on its transfer tax page. An online PT-61 form reports the sale.

The firm that closes your sale normally files the form, retires the mortgage and records the deed. Request a written payoff and a draft settlement statement several days early, and compare its tax line with the Henry County bill. Mortgage payoff figures change by the day, so ask the servicer for a good-through date and confirm the number again just before you sign. If the house is held by more than one owner, each one signs, and each needs time to review the statement. Ask the closing office to send the statement to everyone at the same time.

sections.h2: What should a Stockbridge seller do first?
sections.html:
1. Find your deed and parcel number, plus the newest assessment notice and tax bill from Henry County.
  2. Ask the tax commissioner if any city levy for Stockbridge is billed separately from the county amount.
  3. Order a payoff statement from the servicer of your loan and a lien search through the closing attorney.
  4. Gather offers, including one at a direct cash price, and read each for repair credits, closing dates and which side pays the transfer tax.
  5. Deliver the settlement statement to the county before its 90 day window closes.

Do these in order and a cash sale or a listing both move faster, since most delays come from a missing payoff, an unpaid bill or an unrecorded paper. A tidy file also helps you judge offers fairly, because you will know what you owe before a buyer asks.

faqs.a: Yes. The Henry County Tax Commissioner bills property tax for Stockbridge parcels and keeps an office on Burke Street, and Henry County Schools operate the public schools.

faqs.q: When are Henry County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 16 is the due date, and the bill goes to whoever held the property on January 1. Interest and penalties start after that date, as the county's FAQ explains.

faqs.q: What happens to the tax bill if I sell my Stockbridge house mid-year?
faqs.a: The bill still goes to the January 1 owner. If the county has not received a settlement statement showing where the taxes were paid within 90 days after the due date, it files a lien against that owner.

faqs.q: Do I need to pay a transfer tax to sell in Stockbridge?
faqs.a: Yes, unless an exemption applies. The state collects it before the deed is recorded, and the seller owes it unless the contract says otherwise. The Department of Revenue's transfer tax page states the rate.

faqs.q: Can I sell a house in Stockbridge that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. Plenty of buyers take houses as they are and reduce the price by the repair bill. Weigh two or more offers against what fixing the house yourself would cost.
